source.original_title: 05/30/2026 - Wil Saravia x Andrew Musial KL
source.display_title: 05/30/2026 - Wil Saravia x Andrew Musial KL — Follow Up

call.sequence_note: First closing call; setter Kyla called to confirm the day before — 'yesterday it took a little bit of time for it to come in after I spoke to, a lady called me to confirm. Kyla.' A follow-up was booked for Monday 1 June.

setter.name: Kyla
setter.evidence: 'yesterday it took a little bit of time for it to come in after I spoke to, a lady called me to confirm. Kyla.' — 'Kyla, yeah, she called to confirm.'

prospect.name: Wil Saravia
prospect.occupation: Self-employed mortgage loan officer. Administrative work during the day, client calls and meetings from 5pm to about 8pm; roughly a 10-hour day, seated in front of a computer for most of it.
prospect.family_status: Married to Natalie; two children, a 12-year-old daughter and a 9-year-old son (Gavin). Household finances are joint — 'it's not just my money, it's our money.'
prospect.training_background: Grew up playing sports and was consistently active into his twenties; played baseball as a pitcher. Now trains two to three days a week against a target of four to five, at a crowded local gym or in his backyard with dumbbells used as kettlebells. Plays pickup basketball with a friend his own age and occasionally with much younger players. Has followed Trevor online for about two years and has tried some of the routines himself. Averages an estimated 7,000-8,000 steps a day. Already eats twice a day and fasts regularly for spiritual and physical reasons.
prospect.medical: Right shoulder joint pain that appears only on bench press, which he associates with years of pitching. Right knee has been giving way while walking and climbing stairs for the past three to four weeks — 'you're walking like it just gives' — and it happened again under load the previous day. Undiagnosed and unexamined: 'I got to get that checked out like yesterday' and 'I do have to make an appointment with a doctor to get that checked out.' No clinician has assessed it. Wants to weigh 175-180 lb and to be under 20% body fat.

signals: Wants a former self back explicitly: 'I would love to see my body return, you know, to what it once was'
Dates the loss to a specific hard season — twelve years since the first child, 'since the kids rolled around, it's like, things changed'

Visible regret carried in a concrete image: 'I'm now, I'm the dad in the pool and the beach that keeps the shirt on ... it makes me feel bad about myself, really, because I'm like, nobody else did this. Nobody else is to blame but myself.'
Frames the decision as an admission of defeat rather than an upgrade: 'I've come to the conclusion that I can't do it on my own anymore'
Ten years of failed self-directed attempts and self-diagnosed self-sabotage: 'conveniently, I didn't have time to work out, convenient, you know'

goals.text: Get from 190 lb to 175-180 lb and under 20% body fat
Get stronger again — can no longer lift or push the way he used to
Learn to train for the body he has at 45 rather than the one he had at 20, in 45 minutes not two and a half hours
Take his shirt off at the pool and the beach again in front of his family
Show his kids what maintaining a healthy body looks like and be someone they look up to
Prove to himself he can finally finish the one goal he has never been able to attain — 'this is something that I need to know that I can accomplish'
Have the energy and durability to keep playing basketball without needing a week to recover

pains.text: Cannot stay consistent — trains two to three days against a target of four to five, and 'when other things come up, everything else takes priority'
No fixed training slot in an unstable self-employed schedule that runs from 6am to 8pm
Ten years of effort with almost nothing to show — 'I've been trying for 10 years now, and I see like this much result'
Trains as though he is still 20, then needs a week to recover — 'I'll do a hard workout, but then I need, like, a week of rest'
Self-sabotage driven by fear of repeated failure — 'where I have my insecurities is in failure ... consistent failure, like most people really turns me off'
Shame about his body in front of his own family; keeps his shirt on at the pool and blames only himself
Right knee giving way while walking and on stairs for three to four weeks, undiagnosed and not yet seen by a doctor
Right shoulder pain on bench press dating back to years of pitching
Local gym is crowded enough that he waits for equipment, which erodes the little time he has
Sits in front of a computer for the majority of a ten-hour day

objections.raw_quote: Okay, that's a lot. That's a lot, a lot of money. Way more than I expected. I mean, I want to do it. I mean, at that amount, I definitely, definitely have to get my wife involved.
objections.rep_response: Isolated finances ('is there anything else keeping you from being less than 100% sure that this is what you want to do'), reframed to 'you're not in a should I do it, it's more of a how to pull it off place', then opened the payment-plan conversation and ran the full financial picture.

objections.raw_quote: the conversation where we had is, if it's about, if it's $2,000 or less for the program, go ahead, do it. Anything above that, we have to sit down and talk, because we have to obviously, you know, figure it into the finances.
objections.rep_response: Ran most of the scripted spouse play — 'is there any reason Natalie would not want you to actually be stronger', 'how would she actually react to this', 'why would you put some of the responsibility on her', 'let's say your Natalie is out of equation right now' — and added an unscripted line, 'sometimes it's better to ask for forgiveness than for permission'. Closed on a $100 refundable deposit and a Monday follow-up.

objections.raw_quote: what's stopping me is incurring a $6,000 debt ... as much as I want to do it, I can't do it just blindly. I can't blindside her. I just can't blindside her like that because it's not just my money, it's our money.
objections.rep_response: Countered that it is his health and his physique — 'We're not talking about her, yeah?' — then introduced a three-month tier at $4,000.

objections.raw_quote: I just got to think of how I'm going to make it happen. I just got to, I got to let my brain think a little bit, how I can make it happen. I think Monday, Monday I should have a clear idea.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the delay, booked Monday, and required a $100 refundable deposit to hold the slot.

objections.raw_quote: I got to be honest with you, Andrew. That doesn't sit well with me whatsoever. I mean, I'm a man of my word. If I tell somebody I'm going to do something, I'll do it. I understand your process, so I won't argue it, but that's the one thing in this whole conversation that hasn't sat well with me.
objections.rep_response: Delivered the scripted scarcity rationale — 'we found that with the volume of people that we have coming in, because of how Trevor popular is, we cannot afford to do it that way' — and did not waive the deposit. Prospect paid under protest. Proposed label: deposit_policy_objection.

tiers.note: Improvised live, credited in full toward the six-month programme — 'you only need to come up with another 2K to upgrade after those three months'

offer.payment_plan_terms: No terms were stated. The rep said splitting the payment raises the total — 'if we would split it, that would probably be higher, like if it would be more than two payments' — and confirmed 'if you do more than two payments, the cost increases' without giving any figure, rate or schedule.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Only on the deposit: 'if you come back and you're going to be like, look, I didn't figure it out. I cannot commit to it. We send it right back. So we're not going to be holding to your money, but that's the process.' No programme guarantee was mentioned.

prospect_financials.note: $7,000 in joint savings, which he will not spend down fully; $1,000-1,500 left over in a good month, already earmarked for clothes, savings and incidentals; three to four credit cards with $6,000 total available credit; investments he explicitly ruled out touching. Wife Natalie's stated ceiling for any programme is $2,000.

evidence: No programme payment and no programme link — the only link sent was for a $100 refundable deposit, described in the payment page as 'Kettlebell down payment, $100'
Follow-up booked and confirmed: 'we will talk again Monday at 7 p.m. for the three-month program'
Stated intent short of agreement: 'I'll find a way to come up with the three, not the six ... That's what I'm going to aim for and I will see how I can come up with the money'
Counter-evidence toward closed: he paid the deposit on the call, has followed Trevor for two years, and said 'if it were just my money, yes, I would probably do it in a heartbeat'

Counter-evidence toward lost: his wife has set a $2,000 ceiling on any programme and believes he should do it himself — 'she's probably going to go say you're crazy' — and his entire available credit is $6,000
The close-rule was not applied: he did not verbally agree to purchase, he agreed to try to find the money and to talk again
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call Monday 1 June at 7pm Eastern to decide on the three-month $4,000 option; prospect to work out funding and speak to his wife. On that call (2026-06-01_wil-saravia_andrew-musial) he declined both tiers and the $100 deposit was refunded, so net cash collected for this opportunity is zero.

notable.note: The most complete process execution in the batch and the most concerning outcome. The prospect disclosed a right knee that has been giving way for three to four weeks, said twice that he needs to see a doctor about it, and the rep replied 'okay, so that needs to be checked', then sold a kettlebell programme around it, took a deposit and never returned to the subject. Separately: the prospect's wife had set an explicit $2,000 ceiling on jointly-owned money and the rep's response included 'sometimes it's better to ask for forgiveness than for permission'. A three-month tier at $4,000 was invented on the call, instalments were stated to cost more than $6,000 with no figure given, and the $100 deposit was taken over an explicit and repeated objection from a prospect who works in lending and said the practice does not exist in his own industry.

quality.notes: Frequent short-turn inversions — the rep's questions repeatedly land on Wil's label ('How tall are you?', 'That happens often?', 'Does that make sense?') and Wil's answers on the rep's. Longer passages are correctly attributed, so roles are recoverable throughout. One age inconsistency survives: at 00:02:13 the transcript reads 'I'm 40, I'm turning 45 this year' and he later says 'I'm 45 years old now' and 'before I'm 45'; 45 recorded. Audio garble at the price reveal ('the investment is $6,000. is 홈').
